title: Piwik sending stats to Sonarr
body:
**Description:**

It seems Piwik (piwikCheck.js) is still sending usage stats to sonarr.tv (https://github.com/Radarr/Radarr/blob/develop/src/UI/Shared/piwikCheck.js#L10). Is this supposed to happen?

**Radarr Version:**

0.2.0.386
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: @AeonLucid we can either have these stats, or just remove it. It's up to you since you have access to the server.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
@galli-leo Are you interested in these analytics? If so, let me know and I'll set it up. https://piwik.org/

Looks pretty cool / useful to me.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: @AeonLucid Did you get around to implementing it?

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body: To be honest I think it's a big privacy issue that this is enabled by default and hidden under advanced settings. Users are not even being informed about this.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: While I would usually agree with you, every part of the analytics software is open source: Radarr and Piwiki itself. Also we don't collect any data pertaining to specific users. I specifically disabled ip logging to keep you guys as anonymous as possible. Additionally, you probably leave more data, with just a simple request to our or any other API server, since webservers log ip, user agent, request url, etc.

comments.author: Participant 6
comments.body: @galli-leo Sorry to necro this but I have to agree with @ottowayne. You're collecting a large list of who has radarr installed in one place. Piwik is free software, sure, but that doesn't justify it!

comments.author: Participant 7
comments.body: Turn analytics off if you care that much. It's a user opinion right in settings and the logic statement is right there in the code link above if you want confirmation. Anonymous Analytics are used to find bugs and make Radarr better overall for everyone, but the option is there for those that care. Also couch potato is an alternative if you still feel it's an issue or feel that strongly about it.

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
